newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Govt to announce plans for ECNZ in budget - Bradford.
newsitem.headline: Govt to announce plans for ECNZ in budget - Bradford.

text.p: The government will announce plans for increasing competition in the wholesale electricity generation market in its budget on Thursday, Energy Minister Max Bradford said.
Speaking at an electricity industry gathering in Wellington last night, Bradford said both the industry and the government had roles in increasing competition within the market.
The government would announce its initiatives in the budget, he said.

Asked to elaborate on his comments, Bradford said it was no secret that the officials involved in the establishment of the wholesale power market and the break up of ECNZ into two competing generators, had always believed that a three-way split of ECNZ was preferable.
In June 1995, Contact Energy was split off from ECNZ with 29 percent of the country's generation capacity, and controls were placed on ECNZ's ability to invest in new generation.
Recently the Paris-based International Energy Agency has suggested that the government consider further break-up of ECNZ to encourage greater competition in the wholesale electricity market.
Bradford declined to detail the government's latest plan but he said that ECNZ was clearly frustrated by the constraints on new investment that the break up agreement imposed upon it.

Bradford went on to say that it was important that competition was present in both the demand and supply ends of the electricity market. "The measures that we plan to implement, we believe will do that."

ECNZ has recently argued strenuously against any further break up of the corporation. Among earlier proposals for the break up of ECNZ was a three-way split that would have seen eight small hydro stations, now earmarked for sale, sold as one business.
Bradford said that the sale of those hydro stations was still Coalition government policy.
